tracking.title: Deliver template and optional AI photozine creation with shared consent and export

issues.title: Integrate TideCloak sign-in and authenticated Convex identity
issues.goal: Establish a real authenticated identity across the Next.js workspace and Convex before adding private collection operations.
scope: Provision a Tide realm with three contributor identities and at least three distinct governance administrators; verify the configured sensitive-change threshold requires multiple approvals.
Integrate browser sign-in, session renewal, logout, and Convex token verification using stable subject identifiers.
Document environment variables and enrollment; keep credentials and tokens outside Git.
acceptance: Each demo contributor can sign in and is identified by a stable subject in a protected Convex function.
Unauthenticated, expired, wrong-issuer, and wrong-audience tokens are rejected by protected backend calls.
Logout removes authenticated application access; refresh does not grant a different identity.
Governance setup and pinned server/SDK versions are documented without publishing credentials.
issues.notes: Do not treat a client-supplied user ID or an ordinary database role flag as proof of identity.

issues.title: Prove Tide policies for shared release, revocation, and edition signing
issues.goal: Resolve the cryptographic integration risks before the product depends on an unverified consent mechanism.
scope: Build a minimal encrypted resource requiring two named source approvers, a limited reviewer grant, and a separate named composition recipient.
Establish how approval evidence binds content version, resource, recipient, audience, and processor scope.
Prove an authoritative permission revision and ordering mechanism for withdrawal; separately prove the feasibility of final edition receipt signing.
Attempt a sensitive permission change as one administrator and verify the actual configured quorum blocks it.

Prove named processor-recipient binding and separate manual review/editor permission from explicit transcription, visual analysis, and design processing scopes; a team-controlled model is still a plaintext recipient.
acceptance: A required reviewer can inspect only the assigned resource; an unrelated user cannot decrypt it.
One approval fails to release the source to the editor; both exact approvals succeed.
Database flag tampering, stale evidence, and recipient substitution do not bypass protected release.
The supported revocation semantics and race ordering are demonstrated; any validity-window limitation is explicit.
A signing proof binds a synthetic PDF digest and manifest to all required final approvers; administrative votes do not replace them.
A short integration decision record identifies supported APIs, working versions, limitations, and reproducible real-network checks.
Manual-use approval without the exact processor grant cannot release a source or derivative to that processor; changed recipient, purpose, or derivative type requires fresh consent.
issues.notes: This is a release gate. If a requirement is not supported, revise the architecture and SRD explicitly before downstream work claims it. A mocked policy response does not complete this issue.

issues.title: Extend the Convex model for immutable versions and consent history
issues.goal: Replace the starter schema with the immutable records and references needed by the approved consent design.
scope: Model collection membership, memory versions, composition scopes, actor decisions, permission revision references, candidates, editions, and audit events.
Add indexes and validators; separate mutable workflow projections from authoritative signed evidence.
Define canonical manifest serialization and immutable resource/version identifiers shared by frontend and backend.

Model MediaAsset, ProcessingJob, DerivedArtifact, and DesignPlan records with media type/codec, source and timestamp lineage, processor/model provenance, explicit grant scopes, immutable plan revisions, and full style-influence closure.

Model server AIConfiguration with enabled/default-off state, monotonic revision, operator audit, and processor configuration reference. Store plan template/origin/parent provenance separately from transient editing mode; jobs capture config revision and invalidation state.
acceptance: Content revisions create new records rather than mutating approved source versions.
Required approver sets include uploaders and bind stable identities; unresolved identities cannot be submitted.
Ciphertext and sensitive references are distinct from any intentionally visible routing metadata.
Decision and candidate records retain exact commitments and authoritative revision references.
Retry keys produce one logical mutation, and validation rejects cross-collection references.
Visible and style-only input dependencies and separate editor/reviewer versus processor permissions survive refresh and cannot be silently widened or removed.
Template-built and AI-origin plans share one immutable schema. Operational enable/disable does not rewrite accepted plan provenance, candidate commitments, consent, or final approval evidence.
issues.notes: A schema field named encryptedPayload does not provide encryption. Backend approval projections must not become the authority for protected release.

issues.title: Create collections and manage contributor membership
issues.goal: Let a creator start a collection and admit authenticated contributors without granting unrestricted memory access.
scope: Build collection creation, listing, detail, and a creator-controlled join flow using the existing TanStack workspace.
Implement backend ownership and membership checks, including removal.
Encrypt private collection metadata according to the integration design.
acceptance: A creator can create a titled collection with an occasion; title length is validated.
Three pre-enrolled contributors can join through the controlled flow without email delivery.
A user outside the collection cannot read private metadata or mutate membership.
A join URL alone does not grant source decryption rights.
Removal stops new application-authorized access and does not silently change previously approved audiences.
issues.notes: Keep the creator role separate from contributor consent and administrator governance.

issues.title: Build validated and encrypted image, voice, video, and text uploads
issues.goal: Let contributors submit bounded multimedia memories and declared people without persisting source plaintext remotely.
scope: Build an image/audio/video/text memory editor with local preview or playback, attribution, caption/story, and declared people including speakers; automatically include the uploader.
Enforce SRD signatures, codecs, sizes, duration/dimensions, text limits, twelve active memories, and the collection byte budget. Do not trust extensions or supplied metadata.

Normalize images and remove EXIF/GPS and ancillary location metadata from retained media before encryption; persist no unsanitized original. Explain unsupported codecs or unavailable safe local processing.
Protect source thumbnails and playback, revoke temporary object URLs, and recover interrupted encrypted uploads. In-app recording is outside scope.

Provide protected local video-still selection and manually typed, attributed audio/video excerpts with source time ranges. This deterministic preparation works without transcription, an inference service, or AI credentials.
acceptance: Valid supported JPEG/PNG, audio, video, and text-only inputs create private immutable versions with attribution and required people.
Unsupported/renamed files, SVG, excessive bytes or decoded pixels, over-duration media, unsupported codecs, and over-limit text fail before remote persistence with useful errors.
Retained media have correct orientation where applicable and no ancillary location metadata; remote storage/logs contain no media or private text plaintext.
An unresolved required identity prevents approval submission; unrelated members receive no usable source URL, thumbnail, or playback.
Capability and retry failures preserve recoverable work without claiming a successful upload.
With AI off, an authorized contributor can select a local still and confirm a typed quote without any model dispatch; full source/version attribution is retained.
issues.notes: Use the verified SDK or reviewed envelope design from CH-02; do not introduce an application-held master decryption key.

issues.title: Implement scoped source review and unanimous release policies
issues.goal: Make contribution permissions govern actual resource decryption rather than only interface visibility.
scope: Create resource-specific review grants for assigned approvers.
Bind composition requests to the memory version, collection, required people, editor, review audience, and processor scope.
Require every source approver before release to the named composition recipient.
Implement immutable revision and request validation, including direct-request and replay defenses.

Separate manual editor/reviewer grants from optional grants for each disclosed processor, purpose, input derivative type, and retention disclosure. Enforce each at protected release, including derivatives.
acceptance: Only an assigned approver can obtain the pre-consent review grant for that source.
Missing or declined approval denies release to the editor at the protected operation.
Every correct required approval enables only the exact version and use scope.
Database approval tampering, duplicate actors, stale evidence, substituted recipients, and cross-collection references fail.
Editing content, required people, or processing scope requires a new version/request; membership changes never silently widen access.

Manual approval does not permit AI processing; a pending/declined processor decision blocks transcription, visual analysis, and design requests for that source. Changing processor/scope requires a new request.
issues.notes: Use actual Tide-backed operations for acceptance. Administrative quorum cannot satisfy source contributor consent.

issues.title: Build the contribution approval inbox and revision flow
issues.goal: Give contributors a clear decision about the exact material, private review audience, and proposed use.
scope: Create the source approval inbox with protected previews, attribution, version, editor, audience, and processor disclosures.
Support approve, decline, and request-edit actions, with no mandatory explanation for declining.
Show private, awaiting permission, available, and excluded states to permitted users.
Add protected audio/video playback and exact declared speaker review; show separate manual-use and per-processor decisions with derivative/retention disclosure.
Keep manual-use approval independent of AI consent and availability. Do not make an AI-processing decision mandatory to continue in Template mode.
acceptance: A contributor can inspect the exact image/audio/video/text version, attribution, intended derivatives, editor/audience, and named processor role they are approving.
Approve and decline submit authenticated evidence for the displayed request; silence remains pending.
Requesting an edit produces a new version and the necessary new approval request.
Other members see permission status without private rejection explanations.
Expired sessions, policy denial, duplicate submissions, and refreshes do not falsely show success.
Declining AI processing can leave manual composition available; no processor receives content during limited pre-consent review.
Template creation and source review remain usable when AI is disabled or unconfigured; neither triggers transcription, analysis, or processor setup.
issues.notes: Approval to compose and privately review is distinct from later approval of a downloadable edition.

issues.title: Enforce withdrawals and order concurrent consent operations
issues.goal: Ensure a committed withdrawal prevents later protected releases and official issuance that depend on it.
scope: Implement the authoritative permission revision mechanism proved in CH-02.
Record decision changes and withdrawal history without rewriting prior events.
Invalidate dependent candidates and stop new official downloads under withdrawn grants.
Explain previously released previews and downloaded copies accurately.
Propagate withdrawal through transcripts, frames, visual summaries, cached plans, style-only influence dependencies, queued jobs, late results, and candidates. Order dispatch as a protected release.
acceptance: If withdrawal commits first, a later release or issuance request fails.
If an authorized release commits first, the later withdrawal does not claim to recall that release.
Stale permission revisions cannot issue an edition or authorize a new application download.
After issuance, withdrawal blocks new app-authorized downloads and use in new editions until reapproved.
The interface and tests describe any explicitly accepted revocation validity window; expiry alone is not represented as immediate withdrawal.

A withdrawn style-only source invalidates its dependent design and blocks issuance; queued dispatch is denied and late results discarded. Already dispatched processor exposure is described as irreversible.
issues.notes: An editable Convex status flag alone does not establish the required ordering against a compromised backend.

issues.title: Build Template mode and a shared editor for template and AI plans
issues.goal: Make template creation a complete default path while allowing accepted AI plans to be edited through the same interface.
scope: Build Use a template with at least one complete six-page A5 preset, manual source/still placement and ordering, caption/quote entry, palette/font/layout controls, and recoverable draft state.
Use one DesignPlan validator and preview/editor for template-built, AI-generated, and manually edited plans; consume sanitized backend AI capabilities rather than a client-only toggle.
Keep local still selection and typed attributed source-time-range excerpts available without AI. Require no model key, inference process, or AI consent to create a template draft.
Expose Create with AI/refinement only when server capability and source-processing permission allow it. Show job state and Retry/Continue manually when applicable.
Continue manually preserves the last accepted plan, assets, accepted text, and complete AI/style-source lineage. Do not apply partial/stale results or silently reset to another layout.
acceptance: From an empty draft, create all six template pages with AI disabled and no inference credentials/service; there are zero model calls.
Pending, declined, or withdrawn sources remain excluded; included material has valid editor/reviewer permission and attribution.
Template controls and accepted AI fixture plans use one editor/validator and remain recoverable after refresh; both respect page and resource constraints.
Changing editing mode or disabling AI alone does not mutate accepted plan provenance, frozen PDF bytes, or final approval evidence.
Actual content/layout edits create the required new plan/candidate; changed source meaning requires new source permission.
AI controls reflect server state; a forged/stale client capability never authorizes a backend model call.
Local video stills and confirmed typed quotes work with no automatic transcription or hidden model startup.
issues.notes: Template delivery does not depend on CH-18, CH-19, or CH-21. Use CH-20 fixture plans to prepare the shared editor. CH-18 later supplies live generation/refinement; preserve all influencing source approvers when editing AI-origin drafts manually.

issues.title: Render and freeze exact PDF candidates with content manifests
issues.goal: Produce an immutable candidate that reviewers and eventual downloaders see as the same exact file.
scope: Choose and validate a browser PDF renderer, then embed normalized images and required fonts.

Render a validated template/manual/AI DesignPlan through one engine; freeze exact PDF bytes and canonical manifest with template/origin/schema/renderer/font versions, accepted content, all visible/style-influence dependencies, approvers, audience, and scope.
Encrypt the frozen candidate for its authorized review audience; retain its exact byte sequence.
acceptance: A six-page A5 PDF opens offline in a separate viewer with correct orientation and unclipped captions.
Excluded sources are absent from rendered pages and embedded PDF resources.
A byte change, source change, or scope change produces a new candidate identity.
Partial or failed rendering cannot create an approvable candidate.
A reference render is measured against the provisional thirty-second target, with the device recorded.

Template and synthetic AI-shaped plans render through the same engine with no live inference dependency. Invalid/stale plans cannot freeze; full provenance determines approvers. Live AI integration is verified by CH-18.
issues.notes: No dependency on CH-18 or any inference service: template freeze/approval/download must ship independently. Retain exact frozen bytes; disabling AI alone never rerenders an edition or changes its commitments.

issues.title: Collect final approvals for an immutable downloadable edition
issues.goal: Let every represented contributor approve the exact final photozine and its downloadable, shareable distribution scope.
scope: Build full-candidate private review for the previously authorized audience.
Calculate final approvers from all visible and style-influencing source dependencies, plus authors of new attributed text; display the complete exact candidate for review.
Bind approvals to both PDF and manifest commitments, and invalidate them when the candidate changes.
acceptance: Every reviewer sees the same exact frozen PDF and intended download members.
Approval explicitly acknowledges that the file can be kept, printed, and forwarded outside Chorus.
Missing, declined, stale, withdrawn, or substituted approval prevents official issuance.
Any edit to bytes, included sources, approver set, or download scope creates a new candidate requiring fresh final approvals.
The UI explains that authorized previews can be copied and final approval certifies the official edition rather than providing DRM.

A source that only influenced palette, layout, or headings still contributes required approvers. Regeneration/refinement or withdrawal invalidates the dependent candidate and requires new final review.
issues.notes: A creator or administrator cannot approve for someone else. Reviewer access is already a release and must have been disclosed in composition permissions.

issues.title: Issue policy-authorized consent receipts and verify them offline
issues.goal: Provide verifiable evidence that an exact PDF edition received the required contributor approvals.
scope: Use the policy-governed signing operation proved in CH-02 to authorize issuance.
Bind the receipt to PDF and manifest digests, required evidence, permission revisions, and download scope.
Provide a documented offline verification procedure with trusted verification configuration.
acceptance: Official receipt issuance fails without every required valid final approval and current source dependency.
Direct API calls and database state edits cannot mint a valid receipt by bypassing the policy.
A correct receipt verifies for the exact reviewed PDF; altered bytes or another edition's receipt fail.
A public receipt contains no source plaintext, private rejection explanation, or unnecessary contributor identities.
Retries of an accepted issuance return the existing immutable edition.
issues.notes: Receipt verification demonstrates authorization of a file; it cannot stop an authorized recipient from copying or editing that file.

issues.title: Download approved PDFs with exact-byte and access checks
issues.goal: Deliver the approved photozine to named members as a file that works outside the application.
scope: Implement the official download path with receipt verification, current access checks, and digest validation.
Return the stored approved bytes with a readable filename and optional detached receipt.
Support device saving and ordinary sharing without a recipient Chorus account.
acceptance: Only a currently authorized named member can use the official app download endpoint.
The downloaded PDF digest exactly matches the candidate that received final approval.
Expired or withdrawn permission blocks new app-authorized downloads.
The PDF opens offline on another device, without authenticated asset URLs.
The UI accurately explains that downloaded copies cannot be recalled or forwarding prevented.
issues.notes: Do not implement social publishing, external sharing integrations, or a new PDF render in this endpoint.

issues.title: Add consent history, retry safety, and recoverable errors
issues.goal: Make consent decisions and official issuance understandable and robust during refreshes and interrupted requests.
scope: Expose an authenticated history for decisions, withdrawals, issuance, and download authorization events.
Use idempotent decision/issuance mutations and recover committed results after a dropped connection.
Add actionable errors and redact source contents, credentials, and tokens from telemetry.
Include authorized processing-job dispatch/outcome, derivative invalidation, and design revision history; idempotent retries recover a job while explicit regeneration creates a new revision.
Expose operator AI configuration revisions and job invalidation/cancellation in authorized history, without recording prompts or source payloads. Explain AI-off separately from source withdrawal.
acceptance: History identifies relevant resources, actors, versions, outcomes, and event ordering only to authorized viewers.
Repeated submissions create one logical decision or edition.
A lost response followed by retry recovers the committed result instead of falsely duplicating or claiming success.
A declined decision does not disclose a private explanation to others or in exports.
Logs and error traces contain no source plaintext, decrypted previews, secrets, or full tokens.
Media/transcript/style prompts stay out of telemetry; job errors and invalidation explain recovery without exposing private content.
Disabling/re-enabling AI and invalidating jobs are audited; retry cannot resume an invalidated job or overwrite a newer accepted draft.
issues.notes: Implement idempotency in the earlier endpoint tickets as they land; this ticket completes the cross-flow history and recovery experience.

issues.title: Polish mobile layouts, keyboard access, and PDF performance
issues.goal: Make the complete creation and approval journey usable at the reference widths and on the demo device.
scope: Review collection, upload, approval, composer, final review, and download screens at 360 px and 1280 px.
Add keyboard reachability, visible focus, labels, contrast, textual state descriptions, and pending/error feedback.
Measure rendering and inspect the exported pages; fix clipping and excessive asset size.
Check audio/video review, transcript correction, AI processing disclosures, style controls, refinement, budgets, and job recovery. Record processing/AI latency separately from PDF rendering.
Verify default Template mode, AI-off controls, Continue manually, local media quote/still controls, and accepted-AI draft editing without a model service. Enabled-only polish is an additional pass.
acceptance: All core actions are usable by keyboard with clear focus and labeled controls.
Both reference layouts are readable without unintended page overflow; permission states do not rely only on color.
Invalid files, expired sessions, policy denial, and render failure have useful recovery guidance.
The six-page reference PDF has embedded resources and no clipped captions.
Render timings are recorded against the provisional target, with any remaining deviation documented.
issues.notes: Retain the existing Next.js/TanStack history adapter and verify direct refresh and back/forward after adding workspace routes.

issues.title: Verify the independent template flow and collect dual-mode release evidence
issues.goal: Verify the complete template/consent/export path with AI off, then collect separately recorded AI-enabled and cross-mode evidence for full dual-mode signoff.
scope: Complete the template journey from an empty draft using approved synthetic photos, locally selected stills, and typed attributed excerpts with no AI credentials/service. Inspect network/dispatch evidence for zero model calls.
Run real Tide bypass, withdrawal, governance, exact-byte final-review, receipt, and offline-download checks independently of AI integration.
Verify direct/stale API, background/startup requests, runtime operator authorization, config failure, and disable/re-enable races; test job invalidation with controlled worker fixtures.

Collect real AI-enabled generation/refinement/transcription and cross-mode evidence from CH-18/CH-19/CH-21 after integration. Core template evidence is independently completable; do not label unimplemented AI as tested.
acceptance: AT-01 through AT-26 have separately identified template/off-state and enabled-AI evidence or explicit unmet items. Core template signoff does not depend on inference deployment; complete dual-mode signoff includes all applicable MUST evidence.
Real Tide tests cover missing approvals, policy governance, database tampering, replay, recipient substitution, withdrawal ordering, and final receipt issuance.
AI-off cold start, local media/manual quotes, full template export, and blocked direct/background model requests are demonstrated with no model key or running inference process.
Before full dual-mode signoff, real enabled AI produces distinct valid designs and refinement, and existing accepted plans/PDFs survive disable while stale results are rejected.
A clean setup reproduces template-to-approved-PDF operation. No simulated consent or fixture-only model result is described as implemented real protection/AI.
issues.notes: Template validation can complete while AI integrations are under development. Preserve enabled-only checks as pending evidence, supplied by the corresponding feature tickets; full dual-mode signoff cannot mark those checks passed merely because AI was disabled.

issues.title: Prepare the hackathon demonstration and submission documentation
issues.goal: Show the new possibility clearly: a group creates a keepsake without one administrator controlling every source memory.
scope: Prepare setup/enrollment instructions and a short project overview covering the product, trust constraint, value, TideCloak contribution, and demonstrated behavior.

Record a complete AI-off template creation, blocked source, denied unilateral permission change, final consent, and offline PDF. Add separately verified AI generation/refinement and Continue manually evidence when enabled-mode integration is ready.
Identify mocked external services, implemented protections, known limits, and deferred stretch work.
Document both runtime configurations and the operator AI switch, local manual audio/video preparation, optional inference startup/teardown, and the plaintext exposure of any enabled processor.
acceptance: A teammate can follow the setup and reproduce the demonstration without private credentials in the repository.
The demonstration visibly includes a real protected denial and a successful approved PDF download.
The overview explains the difference between protected source release and copies already received by reviewers or downloaders.
The submission materials match the actual implemented state and the organizer's current instructions.
Product and SRD links, verification steps, and any unmet requirements are easy to find.

An AI-off demo is a supported presentation of the core product; full dual-mode claims include enabled-AI evidence from CH-18/CH-19/CH-21 and cross-mode tests. Explain any unimplemented capability explicitly.
issues.notes: Keep the downloadable photozine primary. The template demo does not require inference. Full dual-mode claims require both paths to be verified; distinguish disabling an implemented feature from omitting its implementation.

issues.title: Add optional-at-runtime AI generation and refinement to the shared composer
issues.goal: Use the authorized memories themselves to create an editable, validated six-page design without requiring a style prompt.
scope: Integrate the CH-21 self-hosted visual/design endpoint; record the exact model/runtime, role, retention, budgets, and deadlines in processor disclosures and provenance. Honor the separate CH-19 transcription scope and keep inference credentials server-side.

Use CH-19 authorized derivatives to infer palette, typography, layout, titles, and editable text. Return one structured six-page plan with short inspiration explanation and complete source/derivative influence closure.
Support an optional style prompt and text refinement; preserve attribution, review quotes, and create immutable plan revisions. Never fabricate memories, alter source photos, or execute model code.

Validate through CH-20 before preview; enforce scopes/current revisions at dispatch and result acceptance. Reject stale/malformed output and expose retry/manual recovery without silent provider fallback.
Integrate the real generation and refinement actions with CH-09; use only bounded resized images, sampled frames, transcripts, and authorized stories, never full raw videos.

Gate every admission/dispatch/refinement/retry on current server AI state/config revision plus exact processor consent; supply the shared editor with immutable accepted plans and preserve Continue manually after disable.
acceptance: Two contrasting authorized multimedia fixture sets generate visibly different coherent designs without a style prompt, using a real disclosed processor.

Only exact currently approved derivative types are sent to the named recipient; manual-only, pending, declined, withdrawn, or cross-collection sources never influence the request through caches or summaries.
The user can inspect inspiration, edit/reject proposed quotes and captions, and refine style by text; every accepted change produces a new plan revision with provenance.
Malformed plans, external URLs, executable markup, unauthorized asset references, missing lineage, overflow, and unreadable contrast fail validation before freezing.
Provider failure, processing decline, quota/budget errors, or invalidation preserve manual editing and do not submit content to another provider.
All style-influencing source approvers remain part of final consent; a withdrawal discards dependent late results and requires regeneration without that source.

Demo processing uses the disclosed team-cloud inference endpoints with service authentication; no managed external AI API is used as an automatic fallback. Endpoint access does not replace contributor consent.
With AI disabled, direct, stale, background, and retry entry points make no model request; missing service credentials do not break Template mode.
Disable invalidates queued/in-flight jobs, late results cannot replace accepted work after re-enable, and fresh jobs require explicit user action and current authorization.
Live AI plans render through CH-10 and remain manually editable when AI is off, retaining all style-only dependencies. Operational toggles alone preserve existing candidate approvals/downloads.
issues.notes: A required implemented capability for the full dual-mode release, optional for each zine and at runtime. No core template/export ticket depends on this issue. CH-21 remains the planned self-hosted inference option; no specific model or external API is selected by this change.

issues.title: Add consented AI transcription and analysis for enabled AI mode
issues.goal: Convert protected multimedia into bounded, reviewable AI inputs without bypassing source or processing consent.
scope: When AI is enabled, integrate the CH-21 transcription endpoint under exact current processor consent and config revision. Consume bounded local image/frame/audio preparation from CH-05; record model/runtime, retention, deadline, and recipient.

Enforce 1280 px visual long edge, twenty-four visuals, twelve memories, 2,000 transcript code points per recording, 12,000 total source-text code points, and the SRD file/duration/collection budgets. Offer explicit selection/reduction instead of silent truncation.
Encrypt immutable derivatives with source/transform versions, timestamp ranges, content commitments, processor provenance, and permission lineage; protect previews and remove temporary buffers.
Provide review/correction of excerpts and declared-speaker attribution. Changed meaning follows source-version consent; no automatic speaker identification.
Enforce ordered dispatch, bounded deadlines and one active AI job per collection, idempotent retries, withdrawal cancellation/invalidation, and rejection of stale late results.
acceptance: Authorized photo, voice, video, and text fixtures produce bounded traceable resized images, stills, and reviewed transcript excerpts.
No transcriber/visual processor receives content before its explicit permission; pre-consent source review triggers no model request.
Over-budget or unsupported media fail with actionable recovery, and users approve any reduced selection; no quote is silently truncated.
Encrypted persistence and telemetry contain no plaintext source/derivative content outside the documented transient processor exposure.
Withdrawal blocks queued dispatch, invalidates cached/in-flight dependent artifacts, and discards late results without claiming to recall already sent content.
Transcript/still selection, source version, and speaker attribution are inspectable before inclusion in the final edition.

Demo processing uses the disclosed team-cloud inference endpoints with service authentication; no managed external AI API is used as an automatic fallback. Endpoint access does not replace contributor consent.

AI-off blocks automatic transcription/analysis and their queued/retry paths. Users can still listen/watch locally, select stills, type attributed excerpts, and complete a template without this integration.
issues.notes: CH-05/CH-09 own non-AI still selection and manually confirmed quotes, so they do not depend on CH-19. CH-21 supplies the planned self-hosted transcriber. All model calls honor CH-22; raw full video remains outside AI requests.

issues.title: Define one DesignPlan contract for templates, manual edits, and AI output
issues.goal: Give the composer, AI integration, and PDF renderer one safe versioned design contract that can be developed independently of authentication.
scope: Define one versioned six-page A5 DesignPlan schema for deterministic templates, manual edits, and AI output, with template/origin/schema versions, authorized asset references, bounded composition, attributed text, optional inspiration, and full influence closure.
Allowlist local cover/image/grid/collage/quote/heading/caption/note components and fonts. Specify renderer input/output, validation errors, immutable revisions, and manifest commitments.
Build synthetic warm scrapbook and bold editorial fixtures plus adversarial plans; validate structural limits, cross-reference membership, geometry, contrast, and text bounds.
Document shared interfaces for CH-09 preview/editing, CH-18 structured output, and CH-10 exact-byte freezing. This is a contract and validation slice, not the full composer or PDF implementation.
acceptance: Both distinct synthetic styles validate and demonstrate that composition can vary while remaining six portrait A5 pages.
Unknown assets/components/fonts, arbitrary HTML/code, network URLs, malformed bounds, wrong page counts, overflow, insufficient contrast, and missing influence references are rejected.
Plan revisions, input lineage, schema/component versions, and commitment rules are documented and usable by all three consumers.
Work runs on synthetic fixtures without credentials or private collection APIs; fixture validation cannot grant real source access.

A complete template plan validates without processor metadata or AI services; AI-origin plans retain immutable processor/source provenance through manual edits. Operational flag changes do not alter canonical plan/PDF commitments.
issues.notes: Independent contract work on synthetic fixtures. Both creation paths consume the same validator/editor/renderer contract; no duplicate PDF engine or authentication edits are required.

issues.title: Provide optional self-hosted inference for AI-enabled creation
issues.goal: Provide a reproducible team-controlled cloud inference stack for transcription, visual analysis, and structured design, verified first with synthetic inputs.
scope: Using the available eight H200 GPUs and English-only demo scope, select and pin models/runtime after checking capability, licensing, VRAM, cost, startup, and budgets. Cloud provider/model/runtime remain open; use separate speech-to-text if needed.

Provide endpoint/adapter contracts for CH-19 transcription and CH-18 visual/structured-design processing, with request limits, model/version provenance, timeouts, health checks, one-job concurrency, and explicit errors.

Use TLS and authenticated endpoints, restricted network access or an authenticated gateway, and server-side service credentials. Endpoint authentication is separate from protected source/processor consent.

Disable prompt/media logging, request-based training, and unintended plaintext persistence in the inference/proxy stack; document temporary-data cleanup and retention. Accepted outputs use encrypted artifact storage.
Benchmark synthetic audio, resized images, video stills, and six-page structured design under SRD budgets. Record output validity and latency separately from PDF rendering.

Document start/stop/teardown, operational plaintext exposure, and manual recovery. No private memories are used before the separate consent integrations work, and no managed AI API is an automatic fallback.
acceptance: A teammate can reproduce the pinned deployment from documented configuration without credentials in Git, with the cloud/GPU and model/runtime/license decisions recorded.
Anonymous inference requests fail; endpoint access is restricted and browser bundles contain no inference credentials.
Synthetic fixtures demonstrate transcription, visual interpretation, and parseable schema-shaped design output; actual plan authorization/validation remains required in CH-18/CH-20.
Logs/traces and persistent temporary storage contain no request/media/transcript plaintext or service secrets; retention and failure cleanup are demonstrated.
Deadlines, concurrency, and media/request budgets are enforced; service failure supports explicit retry/manual recovery and sends no content to a managed fallback.
Documentation acknowledges that the inference process and privileged cloud operators can see authorized plaintext; self-hosting is not claimed to eliminate this trust boundary.
The application builds/starts and completes template creation without provisioning or starting this stack. Runtime AI-off produces no app-originated model requests or inference probes.
issues.notes: Can be developed independently with synthetic fixtures. Inference remains outside the core template dependency graph; live application dispatch integrates CH-22 availability and contributor consent in CH-18/CH-19. Prior model research is a recommendation, not a selected deployment.

issues.title: Add a server-controlled AI switch and safe job invalidation
issues.goal: Let an authorized operator turn all AI processing off while keeping template creation, accepted designs, approvals, and downloads available.
scope: Add an operator-authorized audited runtime AIConfiguration with enabled flag, monotonic revision, processor-config reference, and sanitized public capabilities. Missing/invalid/unreadable config defaults AI to off.

Guard all model entry points: generation, refinement, ASR, visual analysis, startup probes, background jobs, and retries. Recheck current config and exact processor consent at admission and immediately before protected dispatch.

Define ordering for disable versus dispatch; cancel queued work, invalidate in-flight jobs, discard late results even after re-enable, and require a new explicit authorized job rather than automatic resume.

Keep model SDK initialization, credentials, inference health checks, and readiness outside template startup/render/approval/download. Persist accepted plans and frozen candidates independently of transient jobs.

Expose concise disabled/unavailable status and Retry/Continue manually contracts to the composer. Toggle authority cannot change source policy, grant processing consent, or invalidate a valid approved edition by itself.
acceptance: AI-off cold start with no model keys/service supports complete template-to-approved-PDF operation and no app-originated model calls or startup probes.
Direct/stale/forged client requests and automatic retry/background paths cannot dispatch any model work while disabled.
Only authorized operators can change availability; revisions/actions are audited without source plaintext. Read/config failure blocks AI without disabling core template operations.

If disable commits before dispatch, no content is released. Queued and invalidated in-flight results cannot overwrite accepted work, including after re-enable; already dispatched exposure is not claimed to be recalled.
Re-enable requires configured processor roles and fresh user-requested jobs under current contributor consent; it never auto-processes manual drafts.
Existing accepted AI plans remain manually editable, and current candidate approvals/receipts/downloads remain valid subject to ordinary source/access rules.
issues.notes: Can proceed after CH-03 in parallel with collection/upload work; no AI model deployment is required. Shared dispatch hooks are consumed by CH-18/CH-19. Test races with controlled workers before live inference integration.

revision.summary: Template creation and AI-assisted creation coexist through one DesignPlan/editor/PDF engine. Template export has no AI-service dependency. CH-22 adds a server-authoritative runtime AI switch covering all model calls and job invalidation. Existing accepted AI drafts and valid PDFs survive AI-off. CH-01 scope is unchanged; no model/provider is selected by this revision.
